about.text: A firm Tuscan sheep-milk cheese with protected designation of origin since 1996.

sources.text: The first paragraph of its article, shortened.
The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.text: Two types share one rule: the soft fresco is cut small and not cooked, ripened a few weeks; the semi-hard stagionato is cut finer, may be cooked a little, salted longer and ripened four months or more. Only whole sheep's milk of Tuscany and nearby areas may be used.

links.name: Disciplinare di produzione Pecorino Toscano DOP (2014 amendment), ONAF

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.name: break up
steps.note: Broken to hazelnut size for the fresco or maize-kernel size for the stagionato.
Only the stagionato curd may be cooked.

steps.name: mould
steps.note: In moulds, the whey drained by hand pressing or in a steam-heated room.

steps.name: salt
steps.note: Dry or in 17–19 % brine (15–17 °Bé), at least 8 h per kg for the fresco or 12 h per kg for the stagionato.

microbes.name: native, natural or selected lactic cultures

steps.note: At least 20 days for the soft fresco or 4 months for the semi-hard stagionato.
